title: a settings file with the three older JITSO groups gets the file-writes group in one run, and --remove takes all four away
source: intended: docs/decisions.md D8 (setup hook, defect N-17) and A5 (defect N-25): a file with the older three groups is upgraded in one run
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-25, owner answer A5). A file written before the write boundary holds the Bash, orca MCP and SessionEnd groups. `jitso setup hook --yes` strips every JITSO handler and writes the four canonical groups (the new one is `Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` on PreToolUse), with a backup and a diff that shows the new matcher line. A second run is `nothing to do`, and `--remove` deletes the file that held only JITSO groups.

stdout: nothing to do (the guard is already registered in .claude/settings.json)
